_doc: Personal unions between the AI realms (systems/realmUnions.js). Two crowns come to one head when the reigning rulers of two realms are wed to each other (a royal match of their heirs who both came to their thrones, or two crowned rulers wed by their envoys) and the lesser realm's law on the crown abroad (data/laws.json crownAbroad) lets its crown be worn by a king who reigns elsewhere. The greater realm (more land, then the larger host) is the senior crown; its ruler is the MONARCH of both, and the junior realm's own ruler (the consort, later a viceroy) keeps its court. Each realm keeps its own laws, treasury and lords; the monarch speaks for both abroad: they keep the peace with each other, stand allied, the junior realm declares no war of its own, and each joins the other's wars (unless it holds a truce with the foe); when the senior makes peace, so does the junior. The junior's lords resent an absentee king: their TEMPER (0-100) grows weekly (absence, a foreign culture or faith, wars fought for the senior crown, a troubled realm), eased by a consort at home and the monarch's progresses; it sours the realm's stability (stab) and its regard for the senior crown, and past revoltAt the lords may rise and crown a king of their own. A union also ends at a succession that the junior realm's law or blood will not follow: the monarch dies while the consort lives (her crown stays hers), the senior's heir is a regent or a stranger to the blood, a native heir of the junior line comes of age to its throne, or the law forbids a crown abroad. Hash rolls only (world seed + day + key); no RNG stream touched.

text.formed: 👑 {monarch} of {seniorRealm} and {consort} of {juniorRealm} are wed and both reign: the two crowns sit on one head. {SeniorRealm} and {juniorRealm} stand in personal union, two realms with one ruler, their laws and treasuries their own.
text.refused: 🏛️ The lords of {juniorRealm} will have no crown worn abroad: {consort} reigns in {juniorRealm} alone, wed to {monarch} of {senior}, and the two realms stand allied, not one.
text.inherited: 👑 {monarch} succeeds to the throne of {senior}, and by the law of the blood to the crown of {junior} too: the union holds.
text.viceroy: 👑 {old} of {junior} is dead. By the law of the blood its crown passes to {monarch} of {senior}; {resident} keeps the court at {juniorRealm} as regent.
text.partedConsort: 💔 {old} is dead, and the crown of {junior} stays with {consort}, who reigns there in {pos} own right: the union of {seniorRealm} and {juniorRealm} is ended, and the realms part as friends.
text.partedStranger: 💔 {monarch} takes the throne of {senior}, but the lords of {juniorRealm} owe nothing to one not of the blood: they crown {resident}, and the union is ended.
text.partedNative: 💔 The lords of {juniorRealm} crown {resident}, a ruler of their own line, and the union with {seniorRealm} is ended.
text.partedLaw: 💔 By the law of {juniorRealm}, no crown may be worn abroad: {resident} is crowned there, and the union with {seniorRealm} is ended.
text.revolt: 🏴 The lords of {juniorRealm} rise against their absent king {monarch}: they crown {resident}, and the union with {seniorRealm} is broken.
text.reconquest: ⚔️ {monarch} will not let the crown of {junior} go: {senior} marches to take it back.
text.fallen: 💀 With the fall of {fallen}, the union of {seniorRealm} and {juniorRealm} is no more.
text.player: 👑 A new ruler takes the throne of {taken}: the union of {seniorRealm} and {juniorRealm} is ended.
text.joinWar: ⚔️ {junior} joins the war of its king {monarch} on {foe}.
text.joinWarSenior: ⚔️ {monarch} brings {senior} into the war of {junior}, its other crown, on {foe}.
text.peace: 🕊️ {junior} lays down its arms against {foe}, as its king has.
text.progress: 👑 {monarch} keeps court a season at {juniorRealm}: its lords are quieter for it.
text.restless: 🏴 The lords of {juniorRealm} chafe under an absent king: {monarch} rules them from {seniorRealm}.
text.timelineFormed: The crowns of {senior} and {junior} were joined in one head ({monarch}).
text.timelineEnded: The union of {senior} and {junior} was ended.
